framing_b.emotional_framing: The free supply makes the speaker concede that their attempt to avoid the drink is unlikely to last.

parsed.why_different: The laugh embraces the discovery as comic good fortune, while the sigh treats the same discovery as an unwelcome confirmation of a persistent habit.

items.situation: I'll never stop drinking Dr. Pepper.

production_condition_a.when_it_is_produced: When the speaker finds something immediately amusing, delightfully surprising, or warmly absurd; it can also be an affiliative reaction to news.

production_condition_b.when_it_is_produced: When the speaker registers a burden, longing, resignation, or an unwelcome comparison, whether newly learned or already understood.

parsed.shared_moment: The final speaker looks at the friend's newly received shelter photo and recognizes that the dog is the breed they have always wanted.
parsed.what_lands: A photo on the friend's phone reveals the adopted dog's breed to the final speaker in that instant.
parsed.situation_summary: A friend has adopted a dog, and the other speaker discovers it is their preferred breed.
outline: Friend mentions receiving an update from the shelter.
Other speaker asks whether the adoption went through.
Friend says they were sent a photo but has not named the dog.
Friend holds out the phone and asks the other speaker to look.
The other speaker sees the dog, vocalizes, and says, "That's a [breed]. You actually got one."

framing_a.emotional_framing: The discovery becomes a warm, playful moment of delighted disbelief and shared excitement about the friend's good fortune.
framing_a.speaker_state: Amused, pleasantly surprised, and socially engaged.

framing_b.emotional_framing: The discovery highlights the speaker's private wish for the same kind of dog and the unfairness of the comparison.

parsed.why_different: The laugh treats the news as a welcome, playful surprise, while the sigh treats the same news as a reminder of the speaker's own unmet wish.

items.situation: My friend got a new dog. Its my favorite breed so I was a little envious

production_condition_a.when_it_is_produced: An unexpected, immediately perceived development reaches the speaker and interrupts their breath before they can formulate a response.

production_condition_b.when_it_is_produced: The speaker confronts something unwelcome, excessive, burdensome, or exasperating, whether newly discovered or already understood.

parsed.shared_moment: On Christmas morning, the final speaker opens the last package and recognizes that the gifts collectively cover every item they had mentioned wanting.
parsed.what_lands: The final speaker sees the contents of the last opened package and connects it to the other gifts already under the tree.
parsed.situation_summary: A person receives a Christmas collection that fulfills everything they had hoped to get.
outline: Speaker 1 asks whether the final speaker has opened the presents yet.
Speaker 2 says they have opened several but were told to save one package.
Speaker 1 explains that the packages were chosen from things the final speaker had mentioned over time.
Speaker 2 opens the last package and notices it completes the collection.
Speaker 2 sees the final item and says it is every thing they mentioned wanting, with the sound first.

framing_a.emotional_framing: The speaker is struck by the unexpected completeness and generosity of the Christmas gifts.
framing_a.speaker_state: Astonished by a welcome realization.

framing_b.emotional_framing: The speaker sees the gifts as excessive and feels dismayed or embarrassed that so much was spent on them.

parsed.why_different: The gasp treats the discovery as a wonderful surprise, while the groan treats the same generosity as uncomfortable excess.

items.situation: On christmas morning last year, i got everything i wanted.

production_condition_a.when_it_is_produced: When the speaker takes in an unwelcome problem and exhales into the burden of dealing with it; it need not be newly learned.

production_condition_b.when_it_is_produced: When the speaker suddenly encounters startling information or a visible event and reacts at the instant it registers.

parsed.shared_moment: The final speaker sees her daughter open her mouth and, for the first time, notices that a tooth is broken.
parsed.what_lands: The visible broken tooth reaches the final speaker when the daughter opens her mouth after the other caregiver asks her to show it.
parsed.situation_summary: Two caregivers deal with their daughter after she damages a tooth during play.
outline: One caregiver mentions that the daughter had a fall while playing.
The final speaker asks whether she seems hurt or needs attention.
The other caregiver says she has stopped crying but will not say much.
The other caregiver brings the daughter over and asks her to open her mouth for the final speaker.
The daughter reveals the tooth; the final speaker vocalizes, then says the same practical next words.

framing_a.emotional_framing: The discovery becomes another difficult family problem the speaker immediately settles in to handle.
framing_a.speaker_state: Burdened, composed, and preparing to act.

framing_b.emotional_framing: The discovery becomes a sudden, alarming visual realization that interrupts the speaker before they respond.

parsed.why_different: The sigh appraises the injury as an unwelcome responsibility, while the gasp marks immediate shock at seeing its extent.

items.situation: when my daughter broke her tooth

production_condition_a.when_it_is_produced: When a speaker faces a disappointment or inconvenience and exhales in resignation; it may concern something just learned or already understood.

production_condition_b.when_it_is_produced: When a speaker is freshly confronted with an irritating or unpleasant setback, often at the instant its consequence becomes clear.

parsed.shared_moment: At the locked Dairy Queen door, the final speaker reads the posted closing notice after expecting to buy Blizzards.
parsed.what_lands: The final speaker sees the store’s closed notice while checking the door; the companion has just asked them to look.
parsed.situation_summary: Two companions arrive for Blizzards, but the person checking the entrance discovers the shop has already closed.
outline: One speaker suggests stopping for a Blizzard after a long day.
The other says they have been thinking about one all afternoon.
They arrive and notice the parking lot is nearly empty.
One speaker asks the other to check the door because the hours are hard to see.
The checker finds the locked door and closing notice, vocalizes, then reports what they see.

framing_a.emotional_framing: The closure is an unfortunate letdown the final speaker accepts, with weary resignation rather than blame.
framing_a.speaker_state: Disappointed, resigned, and ready to move on.

framing_b.emotional_framing: The closure feels like an especially aggravating thwarting of a wanted treat after making the trip.

parsed.why_different: The sigh treats the closure as a disappointment to accept, whereas the groan treats it as an irritating, immediately objectionable setback.

items.situation: Yesterday, I was really craving Dairy Queen. So, I got in my car and went to grab some Blizzards. When I got there, they were closed.
